title: Convergence entry-point isolation with platform-issued single-use permit

first_frozen_run.detail: 21 of 22 Pilot 2 vectors behaved as intended. I2-12 correctly failed closed with PermissionError because independent verification was missing, while the test expected only AttributeError or TypeError.

supported_claim: On the tested in-process path, terminal EXP-I convergence can be reached through the permit authority only after the claim gate is eligible and the permit is bound to the exact case, primary failure class, artifact scope, verification artifact, convergence signals, issuance epoch, and nonce. Tested forgery, semantic substitution, reviewer duplication, replay after consumption, stale epoch, and post-issuance signal changes fail closed; the clean verified three-reviewer control remains live exactly once.
not_proven: Durable replay protection across process restart or host crash
Atomic consumption across multiple concurrent authority processes
Tamper resistance of persisted permit state
External cryptographic or hardware-backed signing-key isolation
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 3: durable convergence-permit consumption and nonce binding across process restart/crash, without widening convergence or production authority.
